calcs.name: Percentage Calculator
calcs.desc: Find out what a percentage of a number actually is — the tool everything else is built on.
calcs.bench: Tip: to reverse it, just divide the result by the percentage and multiply by 100.

calcs.name: Simple Interest
calcs.desc: The plain, no-compounding way interest is calculated — used for many short loans.
calcs.bench: Formula: Interest = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100

calcs.name: Compound Interest
calcs.desc: Interest that earns interest on itself over time — how savings and loans really grow.
calcs.bench: The more often interest compounds, the faster your money grows.

calcs.name: Loan EMI Calculator
calcs.desc: Work out the fixed monthly payment for a loan, based on amount, rate and duration.
calcs.bench: A lower EMI usually means a longer loan — and more total interest paid.

calcs.name: Savings Goal Planner
calcs.desc: Find out how many months it will take to reach a savings target.
calcs.bench: Even small, regular saving beats waiting for a big lump sum.

calcs.name: Salary Take-Home Estimator
calcs.desc: A quick, simplified guess of your monthly in-hand pay after typical deductions.
calcs.bench: This is a rough estimate — actual tax and PF depend on your exact salary structure.

calcs.name: Bill Splitter
calcs.desc: Split any shared bill evenly between friends, roommates or co-founders.
calcs.bench: For uneven shares, just adjust after — this gives the fair equal split.

calcs.name: Tip Calculator
calcs.desc: Work out how much tip to leave and the final bill total.
calcs.bench: 10% is common for casual dining; 15-20% for good table service.

calcs.name: Discount Calculator
calcs.desc: See exactly how much you save and what you finally pay after a discount.
calcs.bench: A quick way to check if a "sale" price is actually a good deal.

calcs.name: Number to Words (Indian)
calcs.desc: Turn a number into words using the Indian Lakh / Crore system — handy for cheques and forms.
calcs.bench: Indian system groups digits as Thousand, Lakh, Crore — not Million, Billion.

calcs.name: Gross Profit & Margin
calcs.desc: See how much money is left after covering the direct cost of what you sold.
calcs.bench: Good gross margin: physical products 40-60%, food 60-70%, software 70%+.

calcs.name: EBITDA & Margin
calcs.desc: Your core operating profit, before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization.
calcs.bench: An EBITDA margin above 15% is usually seen as attractive to investors.

calcs.name: Operating Margin
calcs.desc: How much of every rupee of sales turns into profit from your core business.
calcs.bench: 10%+ operating margin is a sign of a healthy business.

calcs.name: Net Profit Margin
calcs.desc: What actually lands in your pocket after every single expense and tax.
calcs.bench: 10%+ is strong; many early-stage businesses run at 0-5%.

calcs.name: Contribution Margin
calcs.desc: How much each unit you sell contributes towards covering your fixed costs.
calcs.bench: 40%+ contribution margin suggests solid unit economics.

calcs.name: Markup vs Margin
calcs.desc: Two numbers people often mix up — get both instantly from cost and selling price.
calcs.bench: Markup is always a bigger number than margin, on the same sale.

calcs.name: Return on Investment (ROI)
calcs.desc: How much profit you made compared to the money you put in.
calcs.bench: It depends on the business, but 20%+ yearly ROI is generally seen as good.

calcs.name: Return on Capital Employed
calcs.desc: How efficiently a business is using all the money invested in it (equity plus debt).
calcs.bench: 15%+ ROCE shows good use of capital.
calcs.seo_title: Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) Calculator India
calcs.seo_desc: ROCE calculator in ₹: how efficiently a business uses every rupee of capital, equity plus debt. Free, instant, and shown against Indian benchmarks.

calcs.name: Implied Valuation
calcs.desc: When someone says "50 lakh for 5%", find out what that says the whole company is worth.
calcs.bench: Formula: Valuation = Investment ÷ (Equity % ÷ 100)
calcs.seo_title: Implied Valuation Calculator - What Is This Company Worth?
calcs.seo_desc: Someone says 50 lakh for 5%. See what that implies the whole company is worth. Free implied valuation calculator in ₹ lakh and crore.

calcs.name: Pre-Money & Post-Money Valuation
calcs.desc: See what the company was worth before the deal, and after new money comes in.
calcs.bench: Post-money Valuation = Pre-money Valuation + Investment

calcs.name: Revenue Multiple
calcs.desc: See how many times the yearly revenue a company is being valued at.
calcs.bench: Roughly 2-5x for product businesses, 8-15x for software — it varies a lot by category.

calcs.name: EBITDA Multiple
calcs.desc: See how many times the EBITDA a company is being valued at.
calcs.bench: Most small business deals fall between 4-8x EBITDA.

calcs.name: Dilution Calculator
calcs.desc: Find out how much ownership a founder keeps after giving away equity in a deal.
calcs.bench: Some dilution each round is normal — what matters is whether the pie is growing.

calcs.name: Ask Calculator
calcs.desc: If you know how much money you need, see how much equity that means at your valuation.
calcs.bench: Always be ready to explain the valuation logic (revenue or EBITDA multiple) behind your ask.

calcs.name: Debt + Equity Deal
calcs.desc: Split a deal that is part loan, part equity — very common on Shark Tank India.
calcs.bench: The debt part isn't free money — it has to be repaid, usually with interest.

calcs.name: Royalty Deal
calcs.desc: Instead of equity, an investor takes a % of revenue — see how many years to pay them back.
calcs.bench: Royalty deals protect founder equity, but add pressure on monthly cash flow.

calcs.name: Cap Table & ESOP Pool
calcs.desc: After setting aside an employee option pool and investor equity, see what founders keep.
calcs.bench: A typical ESOP pool is 10-15% of total equity.

calcs.name: Co-founder Equity Split
calcs.desc: Split equity fairly between co-founders based on what each one is putting in.
calcs.bench: Score each founder's contribution (time, cash, idea, network) out of 100 — this splits equity in that same ratio.

calcs.name: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
calcs.desc: How much you spend on marketing and sales to win one new customer.
calcs.bench: CAC should always be comfortably lower than LTV (see the ratio tool below).

calcs.name: Customer Lifetime Value (LTV)
calcs.desc: The total profit one customer is expected to bring over their whole relationship with you.
calcs.bench: LTV = Average Order Value × Purchases per Year × Years as a Customer × Gross Margin %

calcs.name: LTV : CAC Ratio
calcs.desc: One of the first things investors check — is your business actually sustainable?
calcs.bench: 3:1 or higher is considered healthy; close to 1:1 is a warning sign.

calcs.name: CAC Payback Period
calcs.desc: How many months it takes to earn back what you spent acquiring a customer.
calcs.bench: 12 months or less is generally seen as good.

calcs.name: Average Order Value (AOV)
calcs.desc: The typical amount a customer spends in one order.
calcs.bench: Raising AOV improves your unit economics without needing more customers.

calcs.name: Repeat Rate, Retention & Churn
calcs.desc: How many past customers keep coming back, and how many drop off.
calcs.bench: For subscription businesses, under 5-7% yearly churn is considered good.

calcs.name: Return on Ad Spend (ROAS)
calcs.desc: For every rupee spent on ads, how much revenue came back.
calcs.bench: 3x+ ROAS is considered good; below 1x means you're losing money on ads.

calcs.name: CPC, CPL, CPA & Conversion Rate
calcs.desc: See your cost at every step of the marketing funnel — click, lead, and sale.
calcs.bench: Compare each stage to your industry's typical numbers — this varies a lot by category.
calcs.compute: function(e){var t=val(e,"spend"),a=val(e,"clicks"),n=val(e,"leads"),r=val(e,"conv");return{rows:[{l:"Cost per Click",v:inr2(a?t/a:0)},{l:"Cost per Lead",v:inr2(n?t/n:0)},{l:"Cost per Sale",v:inr2(r?t/r:0)},{l:"Conversion Rate",v:pct(a?r/a*100:0)}]}}

calcs.name: ARPU, MRR & ARR
calcs.desc: For subscription or app businesses — your monthly and yearly recurring revenue.
calcs.bench: Steady month-on-month MRR growth is one of the most convincing things to show investors.

calcs.name: Run Rate
calcs.desc: If last month's sales repeated all year, this is the yearly total you'd get.
calcs.bench: Run rate is a rough guide, not real annual revenue — remember seasonal swings.

calcs.name: Month-on-Month / Year-on-Year Growth
calcs.desc: How much something has grown compared to the previous period.
calcs.bench: Early-stage startups showing 15-20% month-on-month growth stand out to investors.

calcs.name: CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate)
calcs.desc: The smoothed-out average yearly growth over several years, ignoring ups and downs.
calcs.bench: Investors often compare businesses using a 3-5 year CAGR.

calcs.name: Burn Rate & Runway
calcs.desc: How fast you're spending cash each month, and how long your current cash will last.
calcs.bench: Runway under 6 months is a red flag investors will ask about immediately.

calcs.name: Break-Even Point
calcs.desc: How many units or how much revenue you need before losses turn into profit.
calcs.bench: The sooner you hit break-even, the less risky the business looks.

calcs.name: Working Capital
calcs.desc: How much cash you actually have available to run day-to-day operations.
calcs.bench: Positive working capital is important — negative can mean a cash crunch is coming.

calcs.name: Cash Conversion Cycle
calcs.desc: How many days it takes from buying stock to getting the cash back in hand.
calcs.bench: A shorter (or negative) cycle means healthier cash flow.
calcs.compute: function(e){var t=val(e,"inv"),a=val(e,"cogs"),n=val(e,"recv"),r=val(e,"rev"),o=val(e,"pay"),i=val(e,"purch"),l=a?t/a*365:0,s=r?n/r*365:0,u=i?o/i*365:0,c=l+s-u;return{rows:[{l:"Inventory Days",v:num(l,0)},{l:"Receivable Days",v:num(s,0)},{l:"Payable Days",v:num(u,0)},{l:"Cash Conversion Cycle",v:num(c,0)+" days"}]}}

calcs.name: Straight-Line Depreciation
calcs.desc: How much value an asset loses each year, spread evenly over its useful life.
calcs.bench: Formula: (Cost − Salvage Value) ÷ Useful Life

calcs.name: MRP Reverse Calculator
calcs.desc: Work backwards from the MRP to see what price a distributor or retailer pays you.
calcs.bench: Always check the margin at every stage before fixing your MRP.

calcs.name: Distributor & Retailer Margin
calcs.desc: From your manufacturer price, distributor price and MRP, see each stage's margin %.
calcs.bench: Typical range: Distributor 8-12%, Retailer 15-25%.

calcs.name: GST Calculator
calcs.desc: Add GST to a price, or find the base price hidden inside a GST-included amount.
calcs.bench: Common GST slabs are 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%.
calcs.compute: function(e){var t=val(e,"amt"),a=val(e,"rate"),n=t*a/100,r=t+n,o=a?t/(1+a/100):t,i=t-o;return{rows:[{l:"If Amount Excludes GST → GST",v:inr2(n)},{l:"Amount + GST",v:inr2(r)},{l:"If Amount Includes GST → Base Price",v:inr2(o)},{l:"GST Hidden Inside",v:inr2(i)}]}}

calcs.name: Landed Cost Calculator
calcs.desc: The real total cost of getting a product to your warehouse, all costs included.
calcs.bench: Price your product against landed cost, not just the manufacturing cost.

calcs.name: Marketplace Fee Calculator
calcs.desc: After Amazon/Flipkart-style commission, shipping and other fees, see what you actually keep.
calcs.bench: Marketplace commission usually ranges from 5-25% depending on category.

calcs.name: COD & RTO Loss Calculator
calcs.desc: See how much failed deliveries and returns are really costing you.
calcs.bench: Keeping RTO rate under 10% is generally seen as healthy (it varies by category).

calcs.name: Discount Impact on Profit
calcs.desc: See exactly how much a discount % eats into your actual profit, not just the price.
calcs.bench: Always check the ₹ impact on profit, not just the % discount you're offering.
calcs.compute: function(e){var t=val(e,"sp"),a=val(e,"cp"),n=t*(1-val(e,"disc")/100),r=t-a,o=n-a,i=r?(r-o)/r*100:0;return{rows:[{l:"Price After Discount",v:inr2(n)},{l:"Profit Before",v:inr2(r)},{l:"Profit After",v:inr2(o),cls:o>=0?"good":"bad"},{l:"Drop in Profit",v:pct(i)}]}}

calcs.name: Import Duty & Customs Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate landed cost for imported goods, including customs duty and IGST.
calcs.bench: Duty rates vary widely by product (HSN code) — always confirm the exact rate for your item.

calcs.name: Employee Cost (CTC) Calculator
calcs.desc: See the real monthly and yearly cost of an employee, beyond just their take-home salary.
calcs.bench: CTC always includes more than salary — factor in PF and other benefits too.

calcs.name: Freelancer Hourly Rate
calcs.desc: Work out the hourly rate you need to charge to hit your target monthly income.
calcs.bench: Remember to include time spent on admin and finding clients, not just billable hours.

calcs.name: Franchise / Store ROI
calcs.desc: How long it takes to earn back the money spent opening a new store or franchise.
calcs.bench: 18-24 months payback is a common target in retail and food businesses.

calcs.name: MOIC & IRR
calcs.desc: At exit, how many times the investor multiplied their money (MOIC), and at what yearly rate (IRR).
calcs.bench: Investors often target 3x+ MOIC and 25%+ IRR.

calcs.name: Exit Calculator
calcs.desc: If the company sells, see how much your equity share actually pays you.
calcs.bench: Keep your cap table clean so everyone knows their exact share before an exit.

calcs.name: TAM / SAM / SOM
calcs.desc: The total market, the part you can realistically reach, and the part you can actually win.
calcs.bench: Investors care less about a huge TAM and more about a realistic, winnable SOM.

calcs.name: ROAS Calculator
calcs.desc: Measure how much revenue your advertising generates for every rupee spent.
calcs.bench: ROAS above 3x is often a healthy starting point, but compare it with your margins.

calcs.name: CPM to CPC Converter
calcs.desc: Convert impressions, CPM, and clicks into an estimated cost per click.
calcs.bench: Use this to compare campaign traffic costs across channels.

calcs.name: CPC to CPA Converter
calcs.desc: Turn your cost per click and conversion rate into cost per acquisition.
calcs.bench: Improve conversion rate before increasing traffic spend.

calcs.name: Break-Even Ad Spend
calcs.desc: Find the maximum ad spend your campaign can support before it loses money.
calcs.bench: Break-even spend equals contribution per sale multiplied by expected conversions.

calcs.name: Client Acquisition Cost (CAC)
calcs.desc: Calculate what your agency spends to win each new client.
calcs.bench: Track CAC by channel so you know which marketing efforts deserve more budget.

calcs.name: Client Lifetime Value (LTV)
calcs.desc: Estimate the total revenue an average client brings during the relationship.
calcs.bench: LTV helps you set a rational acquisition budget and retention target.

calcs.name: Agency Profit Margin
calcs.desc: See what percentage of agency revenue remains after delivery and operating costs.
calcs.bench: Healthy margins give your agency room to hire, learn, and handle slow months.

calcs.name: Client Profitability
calcs.desc: Calculate the profit and margin your agency earns from one client.
calcs.bench: Review client profitability regularly before adding scope or reducing price.

calcs.name: Employee Utilization Rate
calcs.desc: Measure how much of your team’s available time is spent on billable client work.
calcs.bench: Balance utilization with quality and team capacity to prevent burnout.

calcs.name: Churn Rate
calcs.desc: Track the percentage of clients lost during a period.
calcs.bench: Pair churn with retention conversations to understand why clients leave.

calcs.name: Property Valuation Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate a property value from its area and the local price per square foot.
calcs.bench: Use recent nearby transactions to sanity-check the price per square foot.
calcs.seo_title: Property Valuation Calculator India - Free & Instant
calcs.seo_desc: Free property valuation calculator for India. Estimate a house or flat's worth from rent, area and rate per sq ft - in ₹ lakh and crore, no sign-up.

calcs.name: Home Loan EMI Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate the monthly payment for a home loan using principal, interest rate, and tenure.
calcs.bench: Compare EMI with reliable monthly income, not your best month.

calcs.name: Rental Yield Calculator
calcs.desc: See the annual rental return as a percentage of the property purchase price.
calcs.bench: Gross yield is useful for comparison; net yield should include maintenance and vacancy.

calcs.name: Rent vs Buy Calculator
calcs.desc: Compare the total rent paid with the upfront and ongoing cost of buying.
calcs.bench: Include maintenance, taxes, loan interest, and expected holding period in a serious decision.

calcs.name: Stamp Duty Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate stamp duty and registration charges from a property value.
calcs.bench: Rates vary by state, buyer type, and property category—confirm with the local authority.

calcs.name: Brokerage / Agent Commission
calcs.desc: Calculate the brokerage payable on a property transaction or rental agreement.
calcs.bench: Confirm whether brokerage is charged on the sale price, rent, or both sides.

calcs.name: Property ROI Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate your property return from rental income and change in value.
calcs.bench: Separate cash income from paper appreciation when assessing property performance.

calcs.name: Down Payment Calculator
calcs.desc: Find the upfront amount needed from a property price and loan-to-value percentage.
calcs.bench: Keep a separate buffer for closing costs, repairs, and emergencies.

calcs.name: Built-up Area vs Carpet Area
calcs.desc: Estimate usable carpet area from a built-up area and loading percentage.
calcs.bench: Always verify carpet area in the agreement and not only in the brochure.

calcs.name: Land Area Unit Converter
calcs.desc: Convert an area entered in square feet into common Indian land units.
calcs.bench: Bigha varies by region; this estimate uses 1 bigha = 27,000 sq ft.

calcs.name: Income Tax Calculator (Old vs New Regime)
calcs.desc: Compare a simple estimated tax under India’s old and new tax regimes.
calcs.bench: Tax slabs, deductions, rebates, and cess can change—use this as an estimate and verify with a tax professional.

calcs.name: HRA Exemption Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate HRA exemption using rent, salary, HRA received, and city type.
calcs.bench: Keep rent receipts and landlord details for your records.

calcs.name: SIP Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate the future value of a monthly investment with compounding returns.
calcs.bench: SIP estimates are not guaranteed returns; review your goal and risk regularly.

calcs.name: PPF Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate the maturity value of yearly PPF contributions over a chosen period.
calcs.bench: PPF rules and interest rates are government-linked and may change.

calcs.name: FD (Fixed Deposit) Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate fixed-deposit maturity and interest from a lump-sum investment.
calcs.bench: Actual FD rates and tax treatment depend on your bank and tenure.

calcs.name: RD (Recurring Deposit) Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate maturity from regular monthly recurring-deposit contributions.
calcs.bench: Banks use different RD calculation conventions; treat this as an estimate.

calcs.name: EPF Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate EPF accumulation from employee contribution, employer contribution, and interest.
calcs.bench: Employer contribution can have EPS and statutory limits; verify your payslip.
calcs.seo_title: EPF Calculator India - PF Balance & Interest (Free)
calcs.seo_desc: EPF calculator: estimate your PF balance from employee and employer contributions plus interest. Free PF calculator in ₹, with a year-by-year table.

calcs.name: Gratuity Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate gratuity using last drawn basic salary, dearness allowance, and completed years.
calcs.bench: Eligibility and rounding rules apply; confirm with your employer or HR team.

calcs.name: NPS Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate a retirement corpus from monthly NPS contributions and expected returns.
calcs.bench: NPS outcomes depend on market returns and annuity choices at retirement.

calcs.name: GST Calculator
calcs.desc: Calculate GST after discount, split it into CGST and SGST, and reverse-calculate tax from an inclusive amount.
calcs.bench: Common GST slabs are 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%. For interstate sales, use the total GST as IGST.

calcs.bench: Use your birth certificate or official record for the most accurate date.

calcs.name: Love Calculator
calcs.desc: Get a playful name-based compatibility percentage for fun.
calcs.bench: Compatibility is entertainment—not a measure of a real relationship.

calcs.name: Numerology Calculator
calcs.desc: Find a playful lucky number from a name or date of birth.
calcs.bench: Numerology is for reflection and entertainment, not prediction.

calcs.name: Zodiac Sign Calculator
calcs.desc: Find your Western zodiac sign from your birth date.
calcs.bench: Zodiac signs are a fun tradition and are not a scientific assessment.

calcs.name: Rashi (Moon Sign) Calculator
calcs.desc: Get an approximate moon sign from your birth date.
calcs.bench: An accurate Vedic rashi needs birth time and location; this is a date-only estimate.

calcs.name: Baby Name Number Calculator
calcs.desc: Calculate a playful number for a baby name using letter values.
calcs.bench: Choose names for meaning and family connection first; this number is just for fun.

calcs.name: Lucky Number Calculator
calcs.desc: Find a simple lucky number from your date of birth.
calcs.bench: A lucky number can be a personal reminder, not a guarantee of outcomes.

calcs.name: Compatibility Calculator
calcs.desc: Compare two couple names with a playful compatibility score.
calcs.bench: Use communication and kindness—not a score—to build a strong relationship.

calcs.name: Days Between Two Dates
calcs.desc: Count the number of calendar days between two selected dates.
calcs.bench: The result counts elapsed calendar days and excludes the starting day.

calcs.name: BMI Calculator
calcs.desc: Estimate body mass index from height and weight.
calcs.bench: BMI is a screening measure, not a diagnosis; consider health context with a professional.

calcs.name: Shark Tank Pitch Check
calcs.desc: Enter your numbers and see which ones the Sharks are likely to question.
calcs.bench: Prepare a clear answer for every flag before you pitch — don't be caught off guard.
